speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what the Government’s assessment is regarding the risk of vaping devices and equipment being repurposed for the distribution and administration of substances prohibited under the Misuse of Drugs Act; and (b) whether there can be upfront closer collaboration between agencies to address issues arising from vaping devices.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry has studied (i) the relation of vaping with the increased risk of progressing to drug abuse and (ii) the risk of vapes as an apparatus for delivery mechanism for the consumption of a controlled drug; and (b) whether the Ministry will classify vapes as an apparatus or other article under section 9 of the Misuse of Drugs Act given the risk of vapes being misused for drug abuse.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry will consider categorising vapes containing controlled drugs and their associated paraphernalia under the same legal framework as the drugs themselves, imposing similar penalties for trafficking and consumption; and (b) what specific measures are being taken to raise public awareness, particularly among young people, about the dangers of consuming etomidate and other drugs through vapes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These currently form the minority of vape cases in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: CNB takes a zero-tolerance approach towards the consumption of controlled drugs, regardless of how the drugs are consumed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) takes a multi-pronged approach to curb the illicit sale and use of vapes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: HSA works closely with agencies, such as the Singapore Police Force, CNB, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, the National Parks Board and the National Environment Agency, to enforce against vapes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If these agencies detect vaping-related cases in the course of their duties, the cases are referred to HSA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: HSA and CNB work together on the investigations against offenders who use vapes to consume controlled drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) is also working with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to raise awareness about the harms of vaping and encourage our youths to lead a nicotine-free lifestyle.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This complements CNB’s preventive drug education efforts, which aims to raise awareness of the harms of drugs, especially among youths, regardless of how they are consumed.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: She is 13 years old and is worried about vaping catching on in schools.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: A young Clementi resident, 16 years old, told me how they are worried about vaping pods having illegal drugs or even controlled drugs getting into Singapore, because there are advertisements online overseas for how it can be done.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, can I ask the Minister of State two supplementary questions?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: They can be used to fuel nicotine addiction or they could be used to administer controlled illegal drugs; and if so, will the Ministry consider gazetting vaping devices as gateway devices, given they could be used for both on the ground, which is happening in some parts of the world?
Because that will open us up to the risk of foreign drug dealers and foreign drug pushers getting into our heartlands and schools through vapes as a gateway device.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is something that I have shared earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What is key is that we see globally, that there has been a rise in the liberalisation of attitudes and also decriminalisation relating to drug offences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, in Singapore, we continue to have a strong stance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, we are not stopping there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are important efforts that we must take on together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Globally, for drugs, it has become a dangerous setting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But in Singapore, we are also working with like-minded countries to ensure that first, we keep our people safe from the harms of drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we work with counterparts and over time, you realise that even countries which have liberalised their policies, have come to realised that they are not able to control it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I have met my counterparts who shared with me that, it happened very slowly, but it has damaged and destroyed their people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, they are also interested to work with us and we want to get more like-minded people and countries to work together to ensure that not only Singapore is safe but the world will be safer so that we can keep the harms of drugs from our people.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Speaker, Sir, I thank the Minister of State for answering and clarifying section 9 of the MDA.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In June last year, there was a report in the United Kingdom (UK): one in six vapes confiscated in English schools contained illicit drugs.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, I share the concern of Members who raise Parliamentary Questions of vapes being used as a gateway for drug abuse.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Has CNB seen an increase in trend of vapes containing illicit drugs?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand in the Minister of State's clarification and answer just now, that it forms a small proportion of vapes that have been confiscated, but what is the sense of proportion?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Because in that UK report, street drugs were found, ketamine were found.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What kind of drugs are commonly being used or found in vapes?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We continue to work with agencies and our partners and counterparts overseas so that we can not only address this issue, but keep Singapore safe.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I thought he gave a very clear response.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have two supplementary questions and both pertain to youths.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, with reports indicating that youths are aware of the illegality and health risks of vaping, but continue to engage in the practice, what specific measures are the Ministry implementing to address the apparent disconnect between awareness and behaviour among young people?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are relevant issues that we need to address.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, what we do is that we work together with our relevant agencies, not only here, but also our counterparts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, we have very close relationships with our counterparts because drugs move from outside Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we also want to understand how it moves and also what kind of strategies are being adopted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: My colleagues and I often meet our counterparts and we share intelligence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, we make sure that our main purpose is to protect Singaporeans and our country.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But we know that it comes from overseas, as such, they are also interested to work with us to learn from us, how we do things.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, recently, we had the drug Remembrance Day for the victims.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Many of the countries have come forward, especially the ASEAN countries, and they want to learn from us and see how they can work together with us on this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this is not only about us learning from them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is about a partnership, we want to ensure that we keep all people safe and secure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, you also see that youths in most of these countries are the groups that are being affected by controlled drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And the reasons we see from our studies are that at that age, you are more curious, you want to try.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I have met youths who told me that no one is at fault.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Because of their curiosity, they looked at social media and the Internet, and they wanted to experience what addiction is like.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, there are elements of peer pressure and there are inter-generational elements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism, we look at the different efforts to see how we can prevent offending and re-offending and it is also for youths.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to see how we can find new ways and understand the issues better to come up with policies and also, at the same time, work with partners to enhance our efforts in this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is an ongoing landscape and trend that will always change because of the different facets, different directions taken by different countries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But we are very clear in our stance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have a strong stance against drugs and we want to make sure that we protect our people and we want to galvanise our stakeholders and resources within Singapore and outside Singapore, so that while we keep Singapore safe and secure, we keep the countries around us safe so that we are safe and we are able to provide more avenues for a good life for fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Can I ask the Minister of State, how do agencies know in advance if a vaping device – which, by the way, is already illegal – contains nicotine or contains ketamine or some other controlled illegal drug?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Does it depend on how prevalent the substance is?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Can I ask the Minister of State, should we not act now before these controlled drugs in vapes become more prevalent, before they reach the one in six that happened in another country that Member Mr Zhulkarnain highlighted, so as to keep our people safe and to keep our children safe for the future?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also understand the overseas landscape, so, we work together with our counterparts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The nature of drug-related offences or even the kind of investigations we do depends on a lot of intelligence as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it is not as simple as knowing what is controlled or not controlled drugs or nicotine.
